items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: He says, 'Johnnie says, "There's some people over here I want you to meet." ... I went over and he says, "John Simmons, I want you to meet John Hammond."'

ctx.x: Then something happened to Nat, and he wigged out. He says, "Why didn't you all let me know that you didn't want me to be the leader of the band?" So they had to send him back to Los Angeles. They sent the Honeydripper down to take his place, and he took the band over. And the drummer left, and Davey Lewis, out of Kansas City, he was the drummer. He played drums, trumpet, two-finger piano like Lionel Hampton, and the vibes. And through the years, there's been a contro-

versy whether he taught Hamp or not. He says, 'Johnnie says, "There's some people over here I want you to meet." I say, "Yeah, okay." I went over and he says, "John Simmons, I want you to meet John Hammond." Well, I'd never heard of John Hammond, and the trade papers at that time wasn't the DownBeat, it was the Tempo. And I get a wire about three days later to appear at the Old Brunswick recording studios, over here on Weston, for a record date. At that time, Benny Goodman was out here to make "Hollywood Hotel."'

So I showed up. Baby Davey Lewis went with me, he was going to play drums on the date. And who am I there with? Teddy Wilson on piano, Red Norvo on vibes, Harry James on trumpet, Baby Davey Lewis and myself. And I don't know what I'm doing. And people are telling me what a great bass player I am.
